sheets.noticed: A cream page with a mountain profile, '8,000 m' in big serif type, and a red line across it. The look is distinctive and the number pulls me in.
A climber dot creeps along the slope as 'every breath holds' is said. The motion keeps me watching.
'A third of the oxygen' appears in red under the mountain and the dot sits near the red line. The point is clear.
'Your body can't adapt' in bold red. It's a bit dramatic, but the stakes make me stay.
'It is slowly dying, hour by hour' in red, with 'adapt up here' underneath. Grim, and I want to know why.
The same frame, the dot has barely moved, and 'it is slowly dying, hour by hour' is repeated. Nothing new, so I swipe away here.

remembers: Above 8,000 meters every breath holds about a third of the oxygen at sea level, and the body can't adapt, so it is slowly dying hour by hour. Climbers call it the death zone.
